incident_bot: :rotating_light: runtime-prod-gpu-pool-7: multiple OOM events detected (kv_cache pagewalks + allocation failures). 142 affected requests in last 3m. Auto-scaling attempted; some pods failed to recover. Playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/oom-triage. Thread created for live coordination.

james_oncall: on it. switching to on-call view, grabbing logs. customer impact? any 5xxs reported? @liz_support please confirm.

liz_support: we have 6 users filing errors in the last 5m (chat API 500s). Customer affected: 2 trial orgs, 1 paid prod. Support ticket IDs: #RD-5421, #RD-5422. Informing customers about degraded performance.

sara_dev: seeing elevated alloc failures on node r-prod-7a-3: nvml shows repeated CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN then OOM traces. Also kvcache swap counter increased rapidly. Attaching a small log excerpt below.

sara_dev: ```
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] runtime: alloc 1048576 failed at kvcache_store.cc:412
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] runtime: trigger pagewalk, evict candidates: 234
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] nvml: GPU 0 memory reserved 5096MB, used 49512MB, free 2904MB
[2026-03-15T18:02:15Z] runtime: batch_id=0x7f3a evict miss (fragmentation suspected)
```

mike_infra: grabbing dmesg and nvtop. quick check: fragmentation metric estimator shows ~36% fragmentation on r-prod-7a-3 GPU0. Likely many variable-length KV entries plus radial growth in prefix caches.

anya_ml: initial hypothesis: sudden influx of long-context requests caused frequent KV cache allocations with differing prefix sizes -> internal allocator fragmentation + large batch sizes exacerbate peak usage. Two simultaneous factors: (1) request distribution shifted to long tokens, (2) batch coalescing combined heterogeneous sequences into large contiguous allocations.

james_oncall: good hypothesis. live mitigations to try (small and reversible):
- reduce max_batch_size from 16 -> 8 for pool-7
- temporarily enable aggressive_kv_eviction=true
- disable cross-request batching for 10m window (batching_mode=per_user)
- roll a soft restart on 3 of 8 pods in pool-7 to free up fragmented heap
Please ack and implement one-by-one, report effect.

tom_sre: implementing #1 and #2 on a single node now via k8s patch. command: `kubectl -n runtime patch deploy pool-7 --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"MAX_BATCH_SIZE","value":"8"},{"name":"KV_EVICT_MODE","value":"aggressive"}]}]}}}}'`

tom_sre: patch applied to r-prod-7a-3 (pod rolled). Monitoring memory and error rate.

mike_infra: copied nvml snapshot after patch: GPU0 used 42.1GB / 52GB, fragmentation est 24%. Allocation failures dropped on that node. Logs show fewer pagewalk triggers.

james_oncall: good sign. @anya_ml can you validate whether quality/regression risk acceptable for reducing batch size? Any downstream latency spike expected?

anya_ml: reducing batch size will increase per-request latency ~5-12% for small queries, but reduces tail OOM risk significantly. For chat-heavy customers long-turn history cost is dominated by tokens, so minimal quality risk. :thumbsup:

james_oncall: OK proceed to apply same config to remaining 7 nodes in pool-7, staggered 30s between restarts to avoid blast. Also start timeline and hypothesis table in-thread.

sara_dev: starting timeline:
- 18:00:12Z traffic shift detected: 2x long-context burst from analytics customers
- 18:01:05Z first OOM / pagewalk on r-prod-7a-3
- 18:02:30Z incident_bot alert created
- 18:03:00Z on-call paged, support tickets opened
- 18:04:10Z mitigation (node roll + batch reduction) started
- 18:07:45Z alloc failures reduced on rolled node
- 18:09:20Z rolling config to rest of pool in progress

sara_dev: hypotheses (tracked):
H1: KV cache fragmentation from heterogeneous prefix sizes + large batches -> fragmentation + allocation failure
H2: memory leak/regression in new allocator change deployed yesterday (low prior probability, check commit range)
H3: sudden traffic pattern (long-context requests) raised working set beyond typical SLO causing normal eviction to be insufficient

mike_infra: evidence so far: favors H1 and H3. Heap snapshots correspond to many small freed blocks between large used segments. No new allocator commits in last 72h on these nodes (so H2 less likely).

james_oncall: action items assigned:
- sara_dev: compile full heap snapshots + attach kvcache meta stats per node (due +20m)
- tom_sre: finish roll and monitor error rate, note any regressions (ongoing)
- anya_ml: run quick eval on small holdout to measure latency/regression from batch reduction (due +15m)
- mike_infra: gather nvml snapshots and fragmentation estimator across pool (due +10m)
- liz_support: keep affected customers updated, escalate if errors persist (ongoing)

liz_support: notified customers with current mitigation steps and ETA. No requests for rollback so far.

sara_dev: packing logs for post-incident RCA: `/opt/infra/scripts/collect-runtime-oom.sh --nodes r-prod-7a-* --out /tmp/oom-2718281828.tar.gz`. Uploading now to incident folder.

incident_bot: Upload complete: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2718281828/artifacts/oom-logs.tar.gz

tom_sre: full pool rollout completed at 18:12:03Z. Error rate dropped from 2.3% -> 0.15% across pool-7. CPU slightly up but acceptable.

anya_ml: quick eval results: latency median +7%, p95 +10% on chat bench. Quality metrics unchanged on our prompt set. Recommend keeping reduced batch size until fragmentation root cause fixed.

james_oncall: agreed. Next stepsfor RCA:
- collect full allocator histograms and KV prefix distribution for the 24h window around incident
- run targeted repro with mixed-length sequence generator to stress local allocator and observe fragmentation thresholds
- consider long-term: make KV allocator coalescing smarter and add compaction path (low-priority), add runtime flag to prefer contiguous allocations for KV sets

mike_infra: noted. I'll open infra ticket with repro plan and priority P1 until we confirm long-term fix. Ticket RD-INFRA-988.

sara_dev: capturing this thread into the RCA doc and will add timeline + evidence links. Closing live mitigation loop; keeping incident open for RCA.

james_oncall: handing back to follow-up owners. If error rate creeps above 0.5% reopen paging. Good work team. :tada:
